# The labels a text style may be given, and what the parser makes of each one.
#
# `markdown` — the parser reads a complete construct in it: emphasis, code or a
# strikethrough, and the half draws the construct rather than the characters.
# `text` — it does not: the label is ordinary text, and it is drawn as it stands.
#
# The label is parsed as inline Markdown, so what a half draws is what the parser
# reads, and the two halves agree with each other because they ask the same
# parser. The verdicts are what that parser makes of the label: CommonMark with
# GFM's strikethrough, which both halves read.
#
# What makes a construct complete is CommonMark's own question: a delimiter run
# that opens an emphasis may not be followed by whitespace, and one that closes it
# may not be preceded by whitespace.
#
# A label the directive grammar cannot carry — one with a bracket in it — is left
# out of the test: the grammar says a label holds no brackets at all, so the
# directive ends at its name and what follows is ordinary Markdown.

# Strong emphasis.
markdown **Bakery**
markdown **Bakery** is open
markdown A **Bakery** here
markdown **Bakery** and **Coffee**
markdown ***Bakery***
markdown **a*b**
markdown ***a* b***
markdown **Bakery***
markdown *Bakery**

# Emphasis with one asterisk.
markdown *Bakery*
markdown A *Bakery* here
markdown (*Bakery*)
markdown a*b*c
markdown 2 *3* 4
markdown *foo* bar *baz*
markdown **Bakery** *Coffee**

# Emphasis with two underscores.
markdown __Bakery__
markdown A __Bakery__ here
markdown (__Bakery__)
markdown __Bakery__ and __Coffee__

# Emphasis with one underscore.
markdown _Bakery_
markdown A _Bakery_ here
markdown (_Bakery_)
markdown a _Bakery_ b
markdown _foo_ bar _baz_

# Code and links.
markdown `code`
markdown A `code span` here
markdown [text](url)
markdown A [link](https://example.com) here
markdown [text](url "title")

# A delimiter that opens an emphasis may not be followed by whitespace.
text ** Bakery**
text __ Bakery__
text * Bakery*
text _ Bakery_
text **Bakery **
text __Bakery __
text *Bakery *
text _Bakery _
text ** Bakery **
text __ Bakery __

# A delimiter that closes an emphasis may not be preceded by whitespace.
text __Bakery __
text *Bakery *
text _Bakery _

# A delimiter run that is not closed.
text *Bakery
text Bakery*
text _Bakery
text Bakery_
text **Bakery
text Bakery**
text `code
text [text](url

# An underscore does not open an emphasis inside a word.
text snake_case
text snake_case_name
text a_b_c
text x_Bakery_
text x_Bakery_ here
text a__b__c

# A marker on its own, and a pair of them.
text *
text _
text **
text __
text `
text * *
text _ _
text ``

# Brackets on their own are not a link.
text [Bakery]
text [Bakery
text Bakery]
text Bakery](url)

# GFM's strikethrough is a construct, and the label is parsed as Markdown.
markdown ~~Bakery~~

# Ordinary text.
text Bakery
text Baking bread
text 50% off
text a * b * c
text 2 * 3
text a_b
text a*b

# A run of three underscores is emphasis to the parser.
markdown ___Bakery___
markdown _Bakery__
markdown __Bakery_ __

# A run of one asterisk and a run of two is text to the parser.
text a *Bakery**a
text a *Bakery_*a
